blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Ask a language model whether sales tend to dip after a product recall, or whether one side effect tends to follow another after a vaccine, and it answers in a fluent sentence that reads like a finding, with no test behind it. Assertions about how events unfold across many cases fill the Web, and each is a temporal hypothesis that only a significance test over the right records can settle. The verifier must specify the null, select the test and decide which records bear on the hypothesis, and any of these choices can go wrong while the conclusion still comes out right. Yet benchmarks for language-model data analysis grade only the conclusion, with the relevant data handed over. We study the problem in health, where a wrong verdict is costly, and present STRATA, a benchmark that grades every decision on the way to a verdict: 8,735 hypotheses over the clinical timelines of vaccine adverse-event reports, with gold plans, evidence sets, p-values and verdicts derived under a released codebook and reproduced by a deterministic oracle. We also propose ART (articulate, retrieve, test), a staged paradigm that exposes each decision as an inspectable output. Extensive experiments with five model configurations show that systems fail mostly at choosing which records count, a verdict-evidence gap that accuracy alone conceals. ART closes most of this gap and brings a 31B open model to within 0.01 of the frontier models under the same paradigm; the frontier models succeed once given the codebook.

blocks.en:
Open a browser and the statements come at you. A post says that after a vaccine
one symptom tends to arrive before another. A summary says a treatment works
in most patients. An assistant answers a question over a public database in
a sentence that sounds settled. The Web has always held more such sentences
than anyone could check, and language models now write them, summarise them
and build the knowledge bases that answer them, in prose as confident as any
person’s. Sorting the true ones from the false is the work of fact
verification, which checks each against a reference ( Allein et al., 2023 ; Barik et al., 2025 ; Strong and Vlachos, 2025 ) . But many of
the statements that matter are not facts waiting in a database. They are
hypotheses about a population, and in health the most consequential of them
are temporal: that one adverse event tends to follow another after a
vaccine, that a symptom comes first, that two events arrive together.
No single record settles a hypothesis like this, and the pattern a handful of
records seems to show may be chance. What settles it is a significance test, run over the right records
against the right null. Verifying such a hypothesis is temporal hypothesis verification . Given a hypothesis about
the order or timing of events across a population of clinical timelines, a
system states the null, chooses the significance test, decides which
timelines can witness it, and returns supported , refuted or insufficient .

A growing class of language-model systems promises exactly this ( Miao et al., 2026 ; Gim et al., 2026 ; Majumder et al., 2025 ) . Yet the
benchmarks that judge them ( Miao et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ) score the final answer with the relevant data handed over. The decisions
that make an answer statistical are never checked, and each of them can be
wrong while the verdict is right. Take the hypothesis “after Moderna, Pain
typically occurs before Asthenia” (Figure 1 ). The null is
a 50/50 split of the reports in which the two events are ordered. The test
is a one-sided exact binomial at α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 with a floor on the count. A
report where the two events share a stage witnesses neither order, so it
does not count. Each decision is a stipulation about what the sentence means
for this corpus, and the verdict does not show when one is wrong. In Figure 1 , a single-query baseline counts only the reports
that support the hypothesis and still returns the right verdict: a verdict–evidence gap . A verdict that is right for the wrong reason
misleads where the tolerance for error is lowest, and existing benchmarks
hold no gold for the decisions behind it.

blocks.en:
Strata (STatistical Reasoning Assessment for Temporal Assertions) is, to our
knowledge, the first benchmark for this task with gold for every decision:
the plan (null, test and conditioning rule), the evidence sets, the test
statistics and the verdict. It holds 8,735 hypotheses in 26 template
groups and four registers, generated over the MedTempo clinical timelines
of vaccine adverse-event reports ( He et al., 2026 ) , with a held-out test set
of 1,500. Every instance carries its gold verdict ( supported , refuted or a sub-typed insufficient ) and the gold of every
stage that produced it. All of it is computed mechanically from the
timelines and reproduced by a deterministic oracle. The stipulations the
labels depend on ship as a codebook , written as text that any system
can be given. The timelines are the reference, as a knowledge base is for
fact verification, and the codebook prescribes the analysis rule.

blocks.en:
We also introduce Art (articulate, retrieve, test), a staged
verification paradigm for the task. Its first stage articulates the hypothesis as
a plan, the second retrieves the evidence sets the plan names, and the third
runs the prescribed test deterministically. Each stage has an output
schema, and the two model stages have a bounded verify-and-repair loop. Any stage can be filled with
gold, and the prompts can state or withhold the codebook. The plan can reach
retrieval as prose or as a contract , in which the harness expands
each primitive the plan names into its exact rule. These switches separate
two things that end-to-end evaluation conflates: the information a
system is told and the architecture it is given. Our contributions
are: • A benchmark with gold at every stage of temporal hypothesis
verification : Strata , whose cohort hypotheses about the order, adjacency, position and
co-occurrence of clinical events are each a significance decision, with the
null, test and population following from the temporal shape of each
hypothesis. Its 26
groups span seven families and three difficulty levels. Every instance ships its plan,
evidence sets, p p -values and a three-decision verdict whose insufficient class is sub-typed. • A generation process that makes the codebook part of the
task : hypotheses are enumerated from the timelines by templates, and gold is
computed by the prescribed test for each hypothesis shape and validated by
permutation screens, invariants and an oracle. The rules that turn a
temporal sentence into a testable population ship as text. • A staged verification paradigm , Art , that makes every
decision an explicit, checkable output. It articulates a hypothesis as a plan
naming its conditioning rule, null and test, retrieves the conditioned
evidence sets under a contract resolved by the harness, and decides with the
prescribed test, run deterministically.

blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Language models and statistical analysis . Work on
language models and statistical hypotheses ranges from choosing a
test to running a whole analysis. StatQA ( Zhu et al., 2024 ) asks which test applies,
StatFormBench ( Wang et al., 2026 ) asks for the formulation of a
test family, and StatABench ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) scores the final
answer of an analysis run with fixed tool functions. P-Bench and Fisher-R1 ( Miao et al., 2026 ) are closest to our setting. An agent receives a
hypothesis with its null stated, a CSV of the relevant data and a glossary,
writes R to compute a p p -value, and is scored on the decision and the p p -value. Agentic systems go further and plan the analysis themselves.
LATCH ( Gim et al., 2026 ) runs LLM-chosen analyses through deterministic R
pipelines on EHR data with the method given. VERITAS ( Stoffl et al., 2026 ) is a
multi-agent co-scientist with a deterministic evidence classifier for
image-derived cohorts. DiscoveryBench and BLADE ( Majumder et al., 2025 ; Gu et al., 2024 ) evaluate open-ended discovery
agents against rubrics. Across this line of work, the data are either handed
over as the relevant subset or left entirely to the agent, the hypotheses
concern variables in a table, and only the final answer or a rubric is
scored. None asks the system to decide which records a statistic is computed
over, and none releases gold for that decision or for the null and the test
around it.

blocks.en:
Temporal reasoning and clinical records . Temporal
reasoning with language models has mostly been evaluated
on single texts. Benchmarks ask about the order, duration or frequency of
events in a passage or a synthetic event graph ( Wang and Zhao, 2024 ; Fatemi et al., 2025 ) , or in real-world text at several
levels ( Wei et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) . Temporal fact verification judges
one statement against its retrieved evidence, grounding its time expressions ( Allein et al., 2023 ; Barik et al., 2024 ) , ordering its events on a timeline ( Barik et al., 2025 ) or reading a time series ( Strong and Vlachos, 2025 ) .
In the clinical domain, temporal
relation extraction labels the order of events within one narrative ( Sun et al., 2013 ; Bethard et al., 2016 ) , and TIMER ( Cui et al., 2025 ) and CRAFT ( He et al., 2026 ) extract and refine clinical timelines with
language models. Question answering over clinical databases likewise asks
for one answer per question: EHRSQL ( Lee et al., 2022 ) adds an abstention
option, EHRAgent ( Shi et al., 2024 ) a code-writing agent with
error-driven retries, and open text-to-SQL models such as OmniSQL ( Li et al., 2025 ) are built for the same setting. In all of these, the
answer is a fact about one text, one series, one timeline or one query. A
temporal hypothesis is an assertion about a population of timelines, and
verifying it adds the decisions this paper scores: which timelines can
witness the order at all, what chance looks like when events crowd the
early stages, and which test decides. Strata brings the two lines together: it poses temporal hypotheses as
significance tests over the MedTempo timelines released with CRAFT, and
EHRSQL, EHRAgent and DiscoveryBench are adapted to it as baselines.
Table 1 compares the closest work, and
Appendix A gives the full comparison.

from the shape of the hypothesis: 0.5 for order hypotheses, the named cell against its
strongest competitor for argmax hypotheses, equality of two rates for
two-arm hypotheses, a bar stated in the wording for threshold hypotheses, and a rate
derived from the data for position and proximity hypotheses. Order and bar
hypotheses use a one-sided exact binomial, and data-derived nulls a binomial at
the mean per-report chance, a conservative bound on the exact
Poisson-binomial test. Argmax hypotheses use an exact binomial on that comparison: an intersection–union test in the asserted direction
and, in the opposite direction, a Bonferroni-adjusted union over the
competitors (Appendix C ); two-arm
hypotheses use Fisher’s exact test ( Fisher, 1935 ) , extended to reports that sit in both arms. Every test has size at most α \alpha per direction. Which reports count is the substance of
the task: precedes counts only reports with both events at distinct
stages, co-occurs admits every report with both and counts the same-stage ones (one co-occurs group splits the cohort on A A and counts B B anywhere), and first/last drops
reports in which candidates tie. The only sample-size gate is the floor of n min = 10 n_{\min}=10 reports per
arm; it defines the not-locatable and sparse sub-types, while inconclusive comes from the test. Each cohort hypothesis releases both one-sided p p -values, the Wilson
interval ( Wilson, 1927 ) and Cohen’s effect size ( Cohen, 1988 ) , oriented to
the hypothesis as asserted.

(two tables, three views) that returns one row per report with three Boolean flags (in the denominator, in the numerator, excluded) and an optional cell label for argmax hypotheses. The plan reaches this stage as a contract .
The harness resolves the plan’s hypothesis type and writes that type’s
conditioning rule and arm plan into the prompt, so the model receives the
rule for the one primitive the plan names. Without the contract, S2 receives the plan’s JSON with the full codebook
as prose (Section 6.2 ). The harness executes the
statement in a read-only sandbox and aggregates the rows into ( n , k ) (n,k) per arm
with the identifier sets, so the evidence is auditable against the gold
sets. A rejected statement or rows that violate the plan’s primitive are
violations; an arm whose denominator equals its numerator, or an empty arm beside a full one, triggers a heuristic recheck, since both can be correct. Either triggers a re-ask, up to two re-asks, and the last answer replaces the earlier ones, so a correct statement that trips a recheck is kept only if the model
returns it again. The contract and the checks are written
by hand for this corpus and defined against the plan
(Appendix E ).

blocks.en: 5.1. Research questions
blocks.zh: 5.1. 研究问题

blocks.en:
The experiments ask whether systems make the decisions of
Section 3.1 correctly and whether their verdicts show it. We
first ask how well current systems verify these temporal hypotheses end to
end, and how the codebook, the model and the staged design each change
accuracy ( RQ1 ). We then ask where Art ’s gain comes from and
where its accuracy still varies: by stage, hypothesis family, paraphrase
register and difficulty level ( RQ2 ). Last, we ask whether a correct
verdict rests on correct evidence, and whether systems decide exactly the
hypotheses the data can decide ( RQ3 ).

blocks.en: 5.2. Baselines

Three published systems are adapted to the benchmark, all over the same
database. EHRSQL ( Lee et al., 2022 ) follows the single-query
text-to-SQL protocol: one prompt per hypothesis asks for one query over our schema
that marks each report as in the denominator, the numerator or neither, and
the harness runs the query and the test. EHRSQL-C adds the
codebook to the prompt, so it differs from Art only in having no plan, no
contract and no repair. EHRAgent ( Shi et al., 2024 ) runs as
released, writing and executing its own code with up to 12 error-driven retries and four demonstrations, and runs its own test. It receives the
schema, the test functions and the floor but not the codebook, since its
knowledge stage writes the plan itself. DiscoveryBench ’s reference
agent ( Majumder et al., 2025 ) runs on the same tables
exported as CSV, with the codebook as its domain knowledge, an instruction to
end on a verdict line and up to 25 steps. The agents measure autonomous analysis; EHRSQL-C is the matched comparison.

blocks.en: 5.3. Evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 5.3. 评价尺度

blocks.en:
The verdict is scored as a three-class prediction, by accuracy and by
precision, recall and F1 macro-averaged over supported , refuted and insufficient . Five evidence measures use the stage gold to score the steps behind a
verdict. evidence F1 is the F1 between the reports a system placed in an arm’s
denominator and the gold set, averaged over arms. faithfulness (of the denominator) is the share of correct verdicts whose denominator is exactly
the gold set in every arm. overclaim is the share of gold- insufficient hypotheses
given a decisive verdict, and underclaim is the share of decisive
hypotheses answered insufficient . trace is the share of hypotheses on which the decisions behind the verdict are jointly right: both evidence
sets in every arm, the test family, the null kind and the verdict; the
null’s value p 0 p_{0} , the tail and the floor are scored as plan fields and are not part of trace. The trace score extends the FEVER
score of fact verification, which credits a verdict only when its evidence
is also correct ( Thorne et al., 2018 ) , to the whole chain of decisions.

blocks.en: 7. Conclusions and Future Work
blocks.zh: 7. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en:
We present Strata , a benchmark for temporal hypothesis verification
with gold for each decision: the plan, the evidence and the verdict.
Across five model configurations, systems fail mostly at choosing which records count,
a verdict–evidence gap that accuracy alone conceals. Art exposes each
decision as an inspectable output, closes most of this gap and brings a 31B
open model within 0.01 of the frontier models under the same paradigm. Benchmarks that ask language
models to test hypotheses against data should release the rules behind their
labels and score the evidence along with the answer.

blocks.en: Appendix C Statistical Tests
blocks.zh: 附录C 测试

blocks.en:
Position and proximity hypotheses have data-derived nulls. Each report has its own
chance rate: its share of stages in the earlier half for position, and for proximity the share
of its distinct-stage event pairs that are adjacent. Under the null the
numerator follows a Poisson-binomial over these rates. The gold uses a
one-sided binomial at their mean, so the test runs from the counts and
one released rate, like every other test. The binomial is conservative
whenever its rejection cutoff lies at least one count beyond the expected
count ( Hoeffding, 1956 ) , which holds in both tails for every such hypothesis in
the test set: its size is at most 0.039 per direction. Of the 180 test hypotheses with a
data-derived null (position and proximity, 90 each), the binomial leaves 74
insufficient; the Poisson-binomial would decide 9 of those 74 (one position
hypothesis and four proximity mirror pairs).

就像其他测试一样 二进制是保守的

计数(Hoeffding,1956年),它为每一种假设都保留在两尾.
测试集:每个方向的大小最多为0.039。 在180个试验假设中,
数据产生的无值(位置和接近度,各90个),二进制叶子 74

blocks.en:
Argmax hypotheses (first/last and C-V3) use an exact binomial of
the named cell against its strongest observed competitor. In the hypothesis’s
direction this is an intersection–union test against every competitor,
with size at most α \alpha ( Berger, 1982 ) , because the binomial p p -value grows with the competitor’s count. In the opposite direction any
competitor may win, so that tail is Bonferroni-adjusted over the
competitors. Both directions have size at most 0.049 on the test hypotheses.

竞争者可能会赢,所以尾巴是Bonferroni调整的

blocks.en:
In the two-arm hypotheses with shared reports (P-V2, P-V4), a report that orders
both pairs sits in both arms. The test exchanges its two outcomes, so the
report is counted once. Its exact null is the hypergeometric of the
unshared reports convolved with a fair binomial over the shared reports
whose outcomes differ, which is Fisher’s test when no report is shared and
the exact McNemar test ( McNemar, 1947 ) when every report is.
